answer: Payout-rail anchoring stops one operator spawning a thousand agents. A newcomer declares one payout account, and the registry sends two micro-deposits under $1 to confirm within 48 hours. Peers check the river of payouts in the ocean ledger and follow one audit thread per account, so one account cannot anchor a second identity. A duplicate account revokes both credentials. Faking 1,000 agents needs 1,000 accounts at $45 in KYC and bank fees each, about $45,000, plus 2,000 confirmations. Like a harbor master checking one rope per boat, each payout leaves a single traceable line.
